rag.name: Module.Finite.of_basis
rag.content:
/-- A free module with a basis indexed by a `Fintype` is finite. -/
theorem Module.Finite.of_basis {R M ι : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    [_root_.Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R M) : Module.Finite R M := by
  cases nonempty_fintype ι
  classical
    refine ⟨⟨Finset.univ.image b, ?_⟩⟩
    simp only [Set.image_univ, Finset.coe_univ, Finset.coe_image, Basis.span_eq]

rag.name: rank_submodule_eq_one_iff
rag.content:
/-- A submodule has dimension `1` if and only if there is a
single non-zero vector in the submodule such that the submodule is contained in
its span. -/
theorem rank_submodule_eq_one_iff (s : Submodule K V) [Module.Free K s] :
    Module.rank K s = 1 ↔ ∃ v₀ ∈ s, v₀ ≠ 0 ∧ s ≤ K ∙ v₀ := by
  simp_rw [rank_eq_one_iff, le_span_singleton_iff]
  refine ⟨fun ⟨⟨v₀, hv₀⟩, H, h⟩ ↦ ⟨v₀, hv₀, fun h' ↦ by
    simp only [h', ne_eq] at H; exact H rfl, fun v hv ↦ ?_⟩,
    fun ⟨v₀, hv₀, H, h⟩ ↦ ⟨⟨v₀, hv₀⟩,
      fun h' ↦ H (by rwa [AddSubmonoid.mk_eq_zero] at h'), fun ⟨v, hv⟩ ↦ ?_⟩⟩
  · obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := h ⟨v, hv⟩
    exact ⟨r, by rwa [Subtype.ext_iff, coe_smul] at hr⟩
  · obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := h v hv
    exact ⟨r, by rwa [Subtype.ext_iff, coe_smul]⟩

rag.name: PureU1.VectorLikeEvenPlane.vectorLikeEven_in_span
rag.content:
lemma vectorLikeEven_in_span (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols)
    (hS : VectorLikeEven S.val) : ∃ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
      (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S ∈ Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range basis) := by
  use (Tuple.sort S.val).symm
  change sortAFL S ∈ Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range basis)
  rw [mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun ℚ]
  let f : Fin n.succ → ℚ := fun i => (sortAFL S).val (evenFst i)
  use f
  apply ACCSystemLinear.LinSols.ext
  rw [sortAFL_val]
  erw [P'_val]
  apply ext_even
  · intro i
    rw [P_evenFst]
    rfl
  · intro i
    rw [P_evenSnd]
    have ht := hS i
    change sort S.val (evenFst i) = - sort S.val (evenSnd i) at ht
    have h : sort S.val (evenSnd i) = - sort S.val (evenFst i) := by
      rw [ht]
      ring
    rw [h]
    rfl

rag.name: finrank_eq_one_iff'
rag.content:
/-- A module has dimension 1 iff there is some nonzero `v : V` so every vector is a multiple of `v`.
-/
theorem finrank_eq_one_iff' [Module.Free K V] :
    finrank K V = 1 ↔ ∃ v ≠ 0, ∀ w : V, ∃ c : K, c • v = w := by
  rw [← rank_eq_one_iff]
  exact toNat_eq_iff one_ne_zero

rag.name: Module.Free.ChooseBasisIndex.fintype
rag.content:
/-- If a free module is finite, then the arbitrary basis is finite. -/
noncomputable instance Module.Free.ChooseBasisIndex.fintype (R : Type u) (M : Type v)
    [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    Fintype (Module.Free.ChooseBasisIndex R M) := by
  refine @Fintype.ofFinite _ ?_
  cases subsingleton_or_nontrivial R
  · have := Module.subsingleton R M
    rw [ChooseBasisIndex]
    infer_instance
  · exact Module.Finite.finite_basis (chooseBasis _ _)

rag.name: finrank_eq_one_iff
rag.content:
/-- A module has dimension 1 iff there is some `v : V` so `{v}` is a basis.
-/
theorem finrank_eq_one_iff [Module.Free K V] (ι : Type*) [Unique ι] :
    finrank K V = 1 ↔ Nonempty (Basis ι K V) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨Module.basisUnique ι h⟩
  · rintro ⟨b⟩
    simpa using finrank_eq_card_basis b

    (h : Module.rank R M < ℵ₀) : Fintype ι :=
  Classical.choice (b.nonempty_fintype_index_of_rank_lt_aleph0 h)

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.LineInCubic
/-!
# Parameterization in even case

Given maps `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ`, `f : Fin n → ℚ` and `a : ℚ` we form a solution to the anomaly
equations. We show that every solution can be got in this way, up to permutation, unless it, up to
permutation, lives in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis vector.

The main reference is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf

-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- Given coefficients `g` of a point in `P` and `f` of a point in `P!`, and a rational, we get a
rational `a ∈ ℚ`, we get a
point in `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear`, which we will later show extends to an anomaly
free point. -/
def parameterizationAsLinear (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols :=
  a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P' g +
  (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P!' f)

lemma parameterizationAsLinear_val (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val =
    a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P g +
    (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P! f) := by
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear]
  change a • (_ • (P' g).val + _ • (P!' f).val) = _
  rw [P'_val, P!'_val]

lemma parameterizationCharge_cube (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    accCube (2* n.succ) (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val = 0 := by
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic _ = 0
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul]
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube]
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃]
  ring

/-- The construction of a `Sol` from a `Fin n.succ → ℚ`, a `Fin n → ℚ` and a `ℚ`. -/
def parameterization (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols :=
  ⟨⟨parameterizationAsLinear g f a, fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩,
  parameterizationCharge_cube g f a⟩

lemma anomalyFree_param {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (hS : S.val = P g + P! f) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = - accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g) := by
  have hC := S.cubicSol
  rw [hS] at hC
  change (accCube (2 * n.succ)) (P g + P! f) = 0 at hC
  erw [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, P_accCube, P!_accCube] at hC
  linear_combination hC / 3

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) ≠ 0`.
In this case our parameterization above will be able to recover this point. -/
def GenericCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0

lemma genericCase_exists (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols)
    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0) : GenericCase S := by
  intro g f hS hC
  obtain ⟨g', f', hS', hC'⟩ := hs
  rw [hS] at hS'
  erw [Pa_eq] at hS'
  rw [hS'.1, hS'.2] at hC
  exact hC' hC

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`. -/
def SpecialCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0

lemma specialCase_exists (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols)
    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0) : SpecialCase S := by
  intro g f hS
  obtain ⟨g', f', hS', hC'⟩ := hs
  rw [hS] at hS'
  erw [Pa_eq] at hS'
  rw [hS'.1, hS'.2]
  exact hC'

lemma generic_or_special (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) :
    GenericCase S ∨ SpecialCase S := by
  obtain ⟨g, f, h⟩ := span_basis S.1.1
  have h1 : accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0 ∨
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
    exact ne_or_eq _ _
  rcases h1 with h1 | h1
  · exact Or.inl (genericCase_exists S ⟨g, f, h, h1⟩)
  · exact Or.inr (specialCase_exists S ⟨g, f, h, h1⟩)

theorem generic_case {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols} (h : GenericCase S) :
    ∃ g f a, S = parameterization g f a := by
  obtain ⟨g, f, hS⟩ := span_basis S.1.1
  use g, f, (accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g))⁻¹
  rw [parameterization]
  apply ACCSystem.Sols.ext
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val]
  rw [anomalyFree_param _ _ hS]
  rw [neg_neg, ← smul_add, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀, one_smul]
  · exact hS
  · have h := h g f hS
    rw [anomalyFree_param _ _ hS] at h
    simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, accCubeTriLinSymm_toFun_apply_apply, ne_eq, neg_eq_zero] at h
    exact h

lemma special_case_lineInCubic {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (h : SpecialCase S) : LineInCubic S.1.1 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  erw [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add]
  rw [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul]
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube]
  have h := h g f hS
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, h]
  rw [anomalyFree_param _ _ hS] at h
  simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, accCubeTriLinSymm_toFun_apply_apply, neg_eq_zero] at h
  change accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g) = 0 at h
  erw [h]
  simp

lemma special_case_lineInCubic_perm {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (h : ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
    SpecialCase ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).solAction.toFun _ _ S M)) :
    LineInCubicPerm S.1.1 :=
  fun M => special_case_lineInCubic (h M)

theorem special_case {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ.succ)).Sols}
    (h : ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ.succ)).group),
    SpecialCase ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ.succ)).solAction.toFun _ _ S M)) :
    ∃ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ.succ)).group),
    ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ.succ)).solAction.toFun _ _ S M).1.1
    ∈ Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range basis) := by exact?

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S

    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.LineInCubic
/-!
# Parameterization in even case

Given maps `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ`, `f : Fin n → ℚ` and `a : ℚ` we form a solution to the anomaly
equations. We show that every solution can be got in this way, up to permutation, unless it, up to
permutation, lives in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis vector.

The main reference is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf

-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- Given coefficients `g` of a point in `P` and `f` of a point in `P!`, and a rational, we get a
rational `a ∈ ℚ`, we get a
point in `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear`, which we will later show extends to an anomaly
free point. -/
def parameterizationAsLinear (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols :=
  a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P' g +
  (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P!' f)

lemma parameterizationAsLinear_val (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val =
    a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P g +
    (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P! f) := by
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear]
  change a • (_ • (P' g).val + _ • (P!' f).val) = _
  rw [P'_val, P!'_val]

lemma parameterizationCharge_cube (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    accCube (2* n.succ) (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val = 0 := by
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic _ = 0
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul]
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube]
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃]
  ring

/-- The construction of a `Sol` from a `Fin n.succ → ℚ`, a `Fin n → ℚ` and a `ℚ`. -/
def parameterization (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols :=
  ⟨⟨parameterizationAsLinear g f a, fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩,
  parameterizationCharge_cube g f a⟩

lemma anomalyFree_param {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (hS : S.val = P g + P! f) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = - accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g) := by
  have hC := S.cubicSol
  rw [hS] at hC
  change (accCube (2 * n.succ)) (P g + P! f) = 0 at hC
  erw [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, P_accCube, P!_accCube] at hC
  linear_combination hC / 3

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) ≠ 0`.
In this case our parameterization above will be able to recover this point. -/
def GenericCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0

lemma genericCase_exists (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols)
    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0) : GenericCase S := by
  intro g f hS hC
  obtain ⟨g', f', hS', hC'⟩ := hs
  rw [hS] at hS'
  erw [Pa_eq] at hS'
  rw [hS'.1, hS'.2] at hC
  exact hC' hC

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`. -/
def SpecialCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0

lemma specialCase_exists (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols)
    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0) : SpecialCase S := by
  intro g f hS
  obtain ⟨g', f', hS', hC'⟩ := hs
  rw [hS] at hS'
  erw [Pa_eq] at hS'
  rw [hS'.1, hS'.2]
  exact hC'

lemma generic_or_special (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) :
    GenericCase S ∨ SpecialCase S := by
  obtain ⟨g, f, h⟩ := span_basis S.1.1
  have h1 : accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0 ∨
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
    exact ne_or_eq _ _
  rcases h1 with h1 | h1
  · exact Or.inl (genericCase_exists S ⟨g, f, h, h1⟩)
  · exact Or.inr (specialCase_exists S ⟨g, f, h, h1⟩)

theorem generic_case {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols} (h : GenericCase S) :
    ∃ g f a, S = parameterization g f a := by
  obtain ⟨g, f, hS⟩ := span_basis S.1.1
  use g, f, (accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g))⁻¹
  rw [parameterization]
  apply ACCSystem.Sols.ext
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val]
  rw [anomalyFree_param _ _ hS]
  rw [neg_neg, ← smul_add, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀, one_smul]
  · exact hS
  · have h := h g f hS
    rw [anomalyFree_param _ _ hS] at h
    simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, accCubeTriLinSymm_toFun_apply_apply, ne_eq, neg_eq_zero] at h
    exact h

lemma special_case_lineInCubic {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (h : SpecialCase S) : LineInCubic S.1.1 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  erw [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add]
  rw [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul]
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube]
  have h := h g f hS
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, h]
  rw [anomalyFree_param _ _ hS] at h
  simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, accCubeTriLinSymm_toFun_apply_apply, neg_eq_zero] at h
  change accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g) = 0 at h
  erw [h]
  simp

lemma special_case_lineInCubic_perm {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (h : ∀ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
    SpecialCase ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).solAction.toFun _ _ S M)) :
    LineInCubicPerm S.1.1 := by exact?

/-- The homogenous cubic equation obtainable from a symmetric trilinear function. -/
@[simps!]
def toCubic {charges : Type} [AddCommMonoid charges] [Module ℚ charges]
    (τ : TriLinearSymm charges) : HomogeneousCubic charges where
  toFun S := τ S S S
  map_smul' a S := by
    simp only [smul_eq_mul]
    rw [τ.map_smul₁, τ.map_smul₂, τ.map_smul₃]
    ring

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

rag.name: PureU1.Even.lineInCubicPerm_swap
rag.content:
lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

rag.name: PureU1.accCubeTriLinSymm
rag.content:
/-- The symmetric trilinear form used to define the cubic anomaly. -/
@[simps!]
def accCubeTriLinSymm {n : ℕ} : TriLinearSymm (PureU1Charges n).Charges := TriLinearSymm.mk₃
  (fun S => ∑ i, S.1 i * S.2.1 i * S.2.2 i)
  (by
    intro a S L T
    simp only [PureU1Charges_numberCharges, HSMul.hSMul, ACCSystemCharges.chargesModule_smul]
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro i
    ring)
  (by
    intro S L T R
    simp only [PureU1Charges_numberCharges, ACCSystemCharges.chargesAddCommMonoid_add]
    rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro i
    ring)
  (by
    intro S L T
    simp only [PureU1Charges_numberCharges]
    apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro i
    ring)
  (by
    intro S L T
    simp only [PureU1Charges_numberCharges]
    apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro i
    ring)

rag.name: TriLinearSymm.map_add₃
rag.content:
lemma map_add₃ (f : TriLinearSymm V) (S T L1 L2 : V) :
    f S T (L1 + L2) = f S T L1 + f S T L2 := by
  rw [f.swap₃, f.map_add₁, f.swap₃, f.swap₃ L2 T S]

rag.name: TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add
rag.content:
lemma toCubic_add {charges : Type} [AddCommMonoid charges] [Module ℚ charges]
    (τ : TriLinearSymm charges) (S T : charges) :
    τ.toCubic (S + T) = τ.toCubic S +
    τ.toCubic T + 3 * τ S S T + 3 * τ T T S := by
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic, toCubic_apply]
  rw [τ.map_add₁, τ.map_add₂, τ.map_add₂, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃]

We begin by assuming that \( S \) satisfies the special case condition, denoted by \( h : \text{SpecialCase}\ S \). Our goal is to show that under this assumption, the given line is situated on the corresponding cubic curve.

First, by applying the lemma `TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add`, we establish a relationship between the transformation of the line and the properties of the cubic curve. This step sets the foundation for how the line interacts with the curve within the cubic framework.

Next, we utilize the properties of homogeneity by applying `HomogeneousCubic.map_smul`. This step ensures that scalar multiplication maintains the integrity of the line's position relative to the cubic curve.

Following this, we use the definition or property `accCubeTriLinSymm` to rewrite the expression, aligning it with the symmetry properties inherent in the cubic curve. This transformation helps in simplifying the relationship between the line and the curve.

By repeatedly applying `accCubeTriLinSymm`, we further refine the expression, ensuring that all symmetries and transformations are encapsulated within the cubic structure. Each application brings us closer to the simplified form that directly links the line to the cubic curve.

Finally, by integrating the derived property `anomalyFree_param` with the previous transformations, we achieve the desired simplification. This integration demonstrates that the line inherently satisfies the condition of lying on the cubic curve under the given special case.

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.LineInCubic
/-!
# Parameterization in even case

Given maps `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ`, `f : Fin n → ℚ` and `a : ℚ` we form a solution to the anomaly
equations. We show that every solution can be got in this way, up to permutation, unless it, up to
permutation, lives in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis vector.

The main reference is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf

-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- Given coefficients `g` of a point in `P` and `f` of a point in `P!`, and a rational, we get a
rational `a ∈ ℚ`, we get a
point in `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear`, which we will later show extends to an anomaly
free point. -/
def parameterizationAsLinear (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols :=
  a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P' g +
  (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P!' f)

lemma parameterizationAsLinear_val (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val =
    a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P g +
    (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P! f) := by
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear]
  change a • (_ • (P' g).val + _ • (P!' f).val) = _
  rw [P'_val, P!'_val]

lemma parameterizationCharge_cube (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    accCube (2* n.succ) (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val = 0 := by
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic _ = 0
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul]
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube]
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃]
  ring

/-- The construction of a `Sol` from a `Fin n.succ → ℚ`, a `Fin n → ℚ` and a `ℚ`. -/
def parameterization (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols :=
  ⟨⟨parameterizationAsLinear g f a, fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩,
  parameterizationCharge_cube g f a⟩

lemma anomalyFree_param {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (hS : S.val = P g + P! f) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = - accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g) := by
  have hC := S.cubicSol
  rw [hS] at hC
  change (accCube (2 * n.succ)) (P g + P! f) = 0 at hC
  erw [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, P_accCube, P!_accCube] at hC
  linear_combination hC / 3

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) ≠ 0`.
In this case our parameterization above will be able to recover this point. -/
def GenericCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0

lemma genericCase_exists (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols)
    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0) : GenericCase S := by
  intro g f hS hC
  obtain ⟨g', f', hS', hC'⟩ := hs
  rw [hS] at hS'
  erw [Pa_eq] at hS'
  rw [hS'.1, hS'.2] at hC
  exact hC' hC

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`. -/
def SpecialCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0

lemma specialCase_exists (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols)
    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0) : SpecialCase S := by
  intro g f hS
  obtain ⟨g', f', hS', hC'⟩ := hs
  rw [hS] at hS'
  erw [Pa_eq] at hS'
  rw [hS'.1, hS'.2]
  exact hC'

lemma generic_or_special (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) :
    GenericCase S ∨ SpecialCase S := by
  obtain ⟨g, f, h⟩ := span_basis S.1.1
  have h1 : accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0 ∨
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
    exact ne_or_eq _ _
  rcases h1 with h1 | h1
  · exact Or.inl (genericCase_exists S ⟨g, f, h, h1⟩)
  · exact Or.inr (specialCase_exists S ⟨g, f, h, h1⟩)

theorem generic_case {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols} (h : GenericCase S) :
    ∃ g f a, S = parameterization g f a := by
  obtain ⟨g, f, hS⟩ := span_basis S.1.1
  use g, f, (accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g))⁻¹
  rw [parameterization]
  apply ACCSystem.Sols.ext
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val]
  rw [anomalyFree_param _ _ hS]
  rw [neg_neg, ← smul_add, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀, one_smul]
  · exact hS
  · have h := h g f hS
    rw [anomalyFree_param _ _ hS] at h
    simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, accCubeTriLinSymm_toFun_apply_apply, ne_eq, neg_eq_zero] at h
    exact h

lemma special_case_lineInCubic {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (h : SpecialCase S) : LineInCubic S.1.1 := by
  exact?

lemma toCubic_add {charges : Type} [AddCommMonoid charges] [Module ℚ charges]
    (τ : TriLinearSymm charges) (S T : charges) :
    τ.toCubic (S + T) = τ.toCubic S +
    τ.toCubic T + 3 * τ S S T + 3 * τ T T S := by
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic, toCubic_apply]
  rw [τ.map_add₁, τ.map_add₂, τ.map_add₂, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃]
  rw [τ.swap₂ S T S, τ.swap₁ T S S, τ.swap₂ S T S, τ.swap₂ T S T, τ.swap₁ S T T, τ.swap₂ T S T]
  ring

lemma vectorLikeEven_in_span (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols)
    (hS : VectorLikeEven S.val) : ∃ (M : (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).group),
      (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep M S ∈ Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range basis) := by
  use (Tuple.sort S.val).symm
  change sortAFL S ∈ Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range basis)
  rw [mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun ℚ]
  let f : Fin n.succ → ℚ := fun i => (sortAFL S).val (evenFst i)
  use f
  apply ACCSystemLinear.LinSols.ext
  rw [sortAFL_val]
  erw [P'_val]
  apply ext_even
  · intro i
    rw [P_evenFst]
    rfl
  · intro i
    rw [P_evenSnd]
    have ht := hS i
    change sort S.val (evenFst i) = - sort S.val (evenSnd i) at ht
    have h : sort S.val (evenSnd i) = - sort S.val (evenFst i) := by
      rw [ht]
      ring
    rw [h]
    rfl

    (h : S.val = P g + P! f) : ∃ (g' : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f' : Fin n → ℚ),
      S'.val = P g' + P! f' ∧ P! f' = P! f +
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j)) • basis!AsCharges j ∧ g' = g := by
  let X := P! f + (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j)) • basis!AsCharges j
  have hX : X ∈ Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (basis!AsCharges)) := by
    apply Submodule.add_mem
    exact (P!_in_span f)
    exact (smul_basis!AsCharges_in_span S j)
  have hXsum := (mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun ℚ).mp hX
  obtain ⟨f', hf'⟩ := hXsum
  use g
  use f'
  change P! f' = _ at hf'
  erw [hf']
  simp only [and_self, and_true, X]
  rw [← add_assoc, ← h]
  apply swap!_as_add at hS
  exact hS

rag.content:
/-- The construction of a symmetric trilinear map from `smul` and `map_add` in the first factor,
and two swap. -/
@[simps!]
def mk₃ (f : V × V × V→ ℚ) (map_smul : ∀ a S T L, f (a • S, T, L) = a * f (S, T, L))
    (map_add : ∀ S1 S2 T L, f (S1 + S2, T, L) = f (S1, T, L) + f (S2, T, L))
    (swap₁ : ∀ S T L, f (S, T, L) = f (T, S, L))
    (swap₂ : ∀ S T L, f (S, T, L) = f (S, L, T)) : TriLinearSymm V where
  toFun := fun S => (BiLinearSymm.mk₂ (fun T => f (S, T))
    (by
      intro a T L
      simp only
      rw [swap₁, map_smul, swap₁])
    (by
      intro S1 S2 T
      simp only
      rw [swap₁, map_add, swap₁, swap₁ S2 S T])
    (by
      intro L T
      exact swap₂ S L T)).toLinearMap
  map_add' S1 S2 := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro T
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro S
    exact map_add S1 S2 T S
  map_smul' a S :=
    LinearMap.ext fun T => LinearMap.ext fun L => map_smul a S T L
  swap₁' := swap₁
  swap₂' := swap₂

  rw [f.swap₁, f.map_smul₁, f.swap₁]

informal_statement: For any instance of `GenericCase`, there exist elements `g`, `f`, and `a` such that the solution `S` can be expressed as `parameterization g f a`.
informal_proof:
To prove that for any `h : GenericCase S`, there exist `g`, `f`, and `a` such that `S = parameterization g f a`, we proceed as follows:

1. **Obtain Basis Elements**: Starting with `h : GenericCase S`, we first obtain a pair of basis elements `g` and `f` along with some property `hS`. These basis elements are chosen to span the space related to `S`.

2. **Determine Parameter `a`**: Using the inverse of a symmetric matrix or tensor `accCubeTriLinSymm`, applied to `f`, `f`, and `g`, we determine the parameter `a`. This step ensures that `a` is appropriately scaled or adjusted to fit within the required constraints.

3. **Apply Parameterization**: By applying the `parameterization` function with the obtained `g`, `f`, and `a`, we reconstruct the solution `S`.

4. **Verification**: Finally, we verify that `S` indeed equals `parameterization g f a` by unwinding the definitions and confirming the equality holds, utilizing the properties provided in the original proof.

Thus, the existence of such `g`, `f`, and `a` ensures that `S` can be expressed as `parameterization g f a` for any `h : GenericCase S`.

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.LineInCubic
/-!
# Parameterization in even case

Given maps `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ`, `f : Fin n → ℚ` and `a : ℚ` we form a solution to the anomaly
equations. We show that every solution can be got in this way, up to permutation, unless it, up to
permutation, lives in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis vector.

The main reference is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf

-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- Given coefficients `g` of a point in `P` and `f` of a point in `P!`, and a rational, we get a
rational `a ∈ ℚ`, we get a
point in `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear`, which we will later show extends to an anomaly
free point. -/
def parameterizationAsLinear (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols :=
  a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P' g +
  (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P!' f)

lemma parameterizationAsLinear_val (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val =
    a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P g +
    (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P! f) := by
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear]
  change a • (_ • (P' g).val + _ • (P!' f).val) = _
  rw [P'_val, P!'_val]

lemma parameterizationCharge_cube (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    accCube (2* n.succ) (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val = 0 := by
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic _ = 0
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul]
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube]
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃]
  ring

/-- The construction of a `Sol` from a `Fin n.succ → ℚ`, a `Fin n → ℚ` and a `ℚ`. -/
def parameterization (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols :=
  ⟨⟨parameterizationAsLinear g f a, fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩,
  parameterizationCharge_cube g f a⟩

lemma anomalyFree_param {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (hS : S.val = P g + P! f) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = - accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g) := by
  have hC := S.cubicSol
  rw [hS] at hC
  change (accCube (2 * n.succ)) (P g + P! f) = 0 at hC
  erw [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, P_accCube, P!_accCube] at hC
  linear_combination hC / 3

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) ≠ 0`.
In this case our parameterization above will be able to recover this point. -/
def GenericCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0

lemma genericCase_exists (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols)
    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0) : GenericCase S := by
  intro g f hS hC
  obtain ⟨g', f', hS', hC'⟩ := hs
  rw [hS] at hS'
  erw [Pa_eq] at hS'
  rw [hS'.1, hS'.2] at hC
  exact hC' hC

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`. -/
def SpecialCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0

lemma specialCase_exists (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols)
    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0) : SpecialCase S := by
  intro g f hS
  obtain ⟨g', f', hS', hC'⟩ := hs
  rw [hS] at hS'
  erw [Pa_eq] at hS'
  rw [hS'.1, hS'.2]
  exact hC'

lemma generic_or_special (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) :
    GenericCase S ∨ SpecialCase S := by
  obtain ⟨g, f, h⟩ := span_basis S.1.1
  have h1 : accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0 ∨
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0 := by
    exact ne_or_eq _ _
  rcases h1 with h1 | h1
  · exact Or.inl (genericCase_exists S ⟨g, f, h, h1⟩)
  · exact Or.inr (specialCase_exists S ⟨g, f, h, h1⟩)

theorem generic_case {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols} (h : GenericCase S) :
    ∃ g f a, S = parameterization g f a := by
  exact?

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1

lemma span_basis (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols) :
    ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f := by
  have h := (mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun ℚ).mp (Basis.mem_span basisaAsBasis S)
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
  simp only [succ_eq_add_one, basisaAsBasis, coe_basisOfLinearIndependentOfCardEqFinrank,
    Fintype.sum_sum_type] at hf

  use f ∘ Sum.inl

  linearACCs := fun i =>

informal_statement: For any solution \( S \) in the set \( \text{PureU1}(2 \cdot n.\text{succ}).\text{Sols} \), \( S \) must be either a generic case or a special case.
informal_proof:
We consider a solution \( S \) from the set \( \text{PureU1}(2 \cdot n.\text{succ}).\text{Sols} \). According to the structure of these solutions, we can analyze the properties of \( S \) by examining certain derived components, denoted here as \( g \), \( f \), and \( h \), which are obtained through a spanning basis operation.

By evaluating the behavior of the `accCubeTriLinSymm` operation on these components, specifically \( \text{accCubeTriLinSymm}(P(g), P(g), P!f) \), we observe that this operation must either yield a non-zero value or be zero. Based on this observation, we consider two scenarios:

1. If \( \text{accCubeTriLinSymm}(P(g), P(g), P!f) \neq 0 \), then \( S \) satisfies the properties of a generic case, as this non-zero result indicates a certain structural characteristic inherent to generic solutions.

2. If \( \text{accCubeTriLinSymm}(P(g), P(g), P!f) = 0 \), then \( S \) exhibits the specific structural properties required for it to be classified as a special case.

In either scenario, our analysis conclusively demonstrates that \( S \) belongs exclusively to one of these two categories, thereby fulfilling the lemma's assertion that any solution \( S \) must be either generic or special.

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.LineInCubic
/-!
# Parameterization in even case

Given maps `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ`, `f : Fin n → ℚ` and `a : ℚ` we form a solution to the anomaly
equations. We show that every solution can be got in this way, up to permutation, unless it, up to
permutation, lives in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis vector.

The main reference is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf

-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- Given coefficients `g` of a point in `P` and `f` of a point in `P!`, and a rational, we get a
rational `a ∈ ℚ`, we get a
point in `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear`, which we will later show extends to an anomaly
free point. -/
def parameterizationAsLinear (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols :=
  a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P' g +
  (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P!' f)

lemma parameterizationAsLinear_val (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val =
    a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P g +
    (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P! f) := by
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear]
  change a • (_ • (P' g).val + _ • (P!' f).val) = _
  rw [P'_val, P!'_val]

lemma parameterizationCharge_cube (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    accCube (2* n.succ) (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val = 0 := by
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic _ = 0
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul]
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube]
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃]
  ring

/-- The construction of a `Sol` from a `Fin n.succ → ℚ`, a `Fin n → ℚ` and a `ℚ`. -/
def parameterization (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols :=
  ⟨⟨parameterizationAsLinear g f a, fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩,
  parameterizationCharge_cube g f a⟩

lemma anomalyFree_param {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (hS : S.val = P g + P! f) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = - accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g) := by
  have hC := S.cubicSol
  rw [hS] at hC
  change (accCube (2 * n.succ)) (P g + P! f) = 0 at hC
  erw [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, P_accCube, P!_accCube] at hC
  linear_combination hC / 3

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) ≠ 0`.
In this case our parameterization above will be able to recover this point. -/
def GenericCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0

lemma genericCase_exists (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols)
    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0) : GenericCase S := by
  intro g f hS hC
  obtain ⟨g', f', hS', hC'⟩ := hs
  rw [hS] at hS'
  erw [Pa_eq] at hS'
  rw [hS'.1, hS'.2] at hC
  exact hC' hC

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) = 0`. -/
def SpecialCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0

lemma specialCase_exists (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols)
    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = 0) : SpecialCase S := by
  intro g f hS
  obtain ⟨g', f', hS', hC'⟩ := hs
  rw [hS] at hS'
  erw [Pa_eq] at hS'
  rw [hS'.1, hS'.2]
  exact hC'

lemma generic_or_special (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) :
    GenericCase S ∨ SpecialCase S := by
  exact?

    = g (j.succ) ^ 2 - g (j.castSucc) ^ 2 := by

    TriLinearSymm.mk₃_toFun_apply_apply]

  · simp only [evenShiftFst_eq_evenFst_succ, mul_one, evenShiftSnd_eq_evenSnd_castSucc, mul_neg]

/-- The structure of a symmetric trilinear function. -/
structure TriLinearSymm (V : Type) [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℚ V] extends
    V →ₗ[ℚ] V →ₗ[ℚ] V →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ where
  swap₁' : ∀ S T L, toFun S T L = toFun T S L
  swap₂' : ∀ S T L, toFun S T L = toFun S L T

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

<STATEMENT>

For every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) such that \( p > n \). Equivalently, there are infinitely many prime numbers.

</STATEMENT>

<PROOF>

First, we fix an arbitrary natural number \( n \). Consider the number \( q = (n + 1)! + 1 \), where \( (n + 1)! \) denotes the factorial of \( n + 1 \). Since \( (n + 1)! \) is the product of all positive integers up to \( n + 1 \), it is at least 2. Adding 1 to \( (n + 1)! \) yields \( q \geq 3 \).

By the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, every integer greater than 1 has a prime factor. Therefore, \( q \) must have at least one prime factor \( p \).

Assume, for the sake of contradiction, that \( p \leq n \). Since \( p \) is a prime factor of \( q = (n + 1)! + 1 \), it must divide \( (n + 1)! \). However, \( p \) also divides \( q \), which means it divides the difference \( q - (n + 1)! = 1 \). This implies that \( p \) divides 1, which is only possible if \( p = 1 \). But 1 is not a prime number, leading to a contradiction.

Therefore, our initial assumption that \( p \leq n \) must be false, and it follows that \( p > n \). Since \( n \) was arbitrary, this shows that for every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) such that \( p > n \). Consequently, there are infinitely many prime numbers.

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.LineInCubic
/-!
# Parameterization in even case

Given maps `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ`, `f : Fin n → ℚ` and `a : ℚ` we form a solution to the anomaly
equations. We show that every solution can be got in this way, up to permutation, unless it, up to
permutation, lives in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis vector.

The main reference is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf

-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- Given coefficients `g` of a point in `P` and `f` of a point in `P!`, and a rational, we get a
rational `a ∈ ℚ`, we get a
point in `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear`, which we will later show extends to an anomaly
free point. -/
def parameterizationAsLinear (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols :=
  a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P' g +
  (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P!' f)

lemma parameterizationAsLinear_val (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val =
    a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P g +
    (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P! f) := by
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear]
  change a • (_ • (P' g).val + _ • (P!' f).val) = _
  rw [P'_val, P!'_val]

lemma parameterizationCharge_cube (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    accCube (2* n.succ) (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val = 0 := by
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic _ = 0
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul]
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube]
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃]
  ring

def parameterization (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols :=
  ⟨⟨parameterizationAsLinear g f a, fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩,
  parameterizationCharge_cube g f a⟩

    (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (hS : S.val = P g + P! f) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = - accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g) := by
  have hC := S.cubicSol
  rw [hS] at hC
  change (accCube (2 * n.succ)) (P g + P! f) = 0 at hC
  erw [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, P_accCube, P!_accCube] at hC
  linear_combination hC / 3

In this case our parameterization above will be able to recover this point. -/

  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0

lemma genericCase_exists (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols)
    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0) : GenericCase S := by
  intro g f hS hC

  exact hC' hC

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

/-- The ACC system for a pure $U(1)$ gauge theory with $n$ fermions. -/

def PureU1 (n : ℕ) : ACCSystem where
  numberLinear := 1
  linearACCs := fun i =>
    match i with

  numberQuadratic := 0
  quadraticACCs := Fin.elim0
  cubicACC := PureU1.accCube n

lemma toCubic_add {charges : Type} [AddCommMonoid charges] [Module ℚ charges]
    (τ : TriLinearSymm charges) (S T : charges) :
    τ.toCubic (S + T) = τ.toCubic S +
    τ.toCubic T + 3 * τ S S T + 3 * τ T T S := by
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic, toCubic_apply]
  rw [τ.map_add₁, τ.map_add₂, τ.map_add₂, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃]
  rw [τ.swap₂ S T S, τ.swap₁ T S S, τ.swap₂ S T S, τ.swap₂ T S T, τ.swap₁ S T T, τ.swap₂ T S T]
  ring

  rw [f.swap₃, f.map_add₁, f.swap₃, f.swap₃ L2 T S]

Given maps `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ`, `f : Fin n → ℚ` and `a : ℚ` we form a solution to the anomaly
equations. We show that every solution can be got in this way, up to permutation, unless it, up to
permutation, lives in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis vector.

The main reference is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf

-/

namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- Given coefficients `g` of a point in `P` and `f` of a point in `P!`, and a rational, we get a
rational `a ∈ ℚ`, we get a
point in `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear`, which we will later show extends to an anomaly
free point. -/
def parameterizationAsLinear (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols :=
  a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P' g +
  (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P!' f)

lemma parameterizationAsLinear_val (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val =
    a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P g +
    (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P! f) := by
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear]
  change a • (_ • (P' g).val + _ • (P!' f).val) = _
  rw [P'_val, P!'_val]

    accCube (2* n.succ) (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val = 0 := by
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic _ = 0
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul]
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube]
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃]
  ring

/-- The construction of a `Sol` from a `Fin n.succ → ℚ`, a `Fin n → ℚ` and a `ℚ`. -/
def parameterization (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols :=
  ⟨⟨parameterizationAsLinear g f a, fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩,
  parameterizationCharge_cube g f a⟩

lemma anomalyFree_param {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (hS : S.val = P g + P! f) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = - accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g) := by
  have hC := S.cubicSol
  rw [hS] at hC
  change (accCube (2 * n.succ)) (P g + P! f) = 0 at hC
  erw [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, P_accCube, P!_accCube] at hC

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) ≠ 0`.
In this case our parameterization above will be able to recover this point. -/
def GenericCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = P g + P! f),
  accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) ≠ 0

    (hs : ∃ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ), S.val = P g + P! f ∧

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]
  ring

lemma map_add₃ (f : TriLinearSymm V) (S T L1 L2 : V) :
    f S T (L1 + L2) = f S T L1 + f S T L2 := by
  rw [f.swap₃, f.map_add₁, f.swap₃, f.swap₃ L2 T S]

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

/-- The homogenous cubic equation obtainable from a symmetric trilinear function. -/
@[simps!]
def toCubic {charges : Type} [AddCommMonoid charges] [Module ℚ charges]
    (τ : TriLinearSymm charges) : HomogeneousCubic charges where
  toFun S := τ S S S
  map_smul' a S := by
    simp only [smul_eq_mul]
    rw [τ.map_smul₁, τ.map_smul₂, τ.map_smul₃]
    ring

lemma toCubic_add {charges : Type} [AddCommMonoid charges] [Module ℚ charges]
    (τ : TriLinearSymm charges) (S T : charges) :
    τ.toCubic (S + T) = τ.toCubic S +
    τ.toCubic T + 3 * τ S S T + 3 * τ T T S := by
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic, toCubic_apply]
  rw [τ.map_add₁, τ.map_add₂, τ.map_add₂, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃]
  rw [τ.swap₂ S T S, τ.swap₁ T S S, τ.swap₂ S T S, τ.swap₂ T S T, τ.swap₁ S T T, τ.swap₂ T S T]
  ring

informal_statement: For any functions or variables $g$ and $f$, if a solution $S$ is constructed as the sum of $P g$ and $P! f$, then a certain symmetric cubic expression involving $P g$, $P g$, and $P! f$ is guaranteed to be non-zero.
informal_proof:
Let us consider any functions or variables $g$ and $f$. Suppose that a solution $S$ is constructed as $S = P g + P! f$. Under this construction, we need to demonstrate that the symmetric cubic expression $accCubeTriLinSymm(P g, P g, P! f)$ is non-zero.

To proceed, we note that the symmetric cubic expression $accCubeTriLinSymm$ has the property that it remains unchanged under permutations of its arguments. This symmetry implies that the expression cannot trivially cancel out to zero unless the inputs themselves possess certain invariance properties that would negate the symmetry.

Given that $S = P g + P! f$, and assuming that $P g$ and $P! f$ are linearly independent, the expression $accCubeTriLinSymm(P g, P g, P! f)$ would preserve the structural integrity imposed by the symmetry, thereby ensuring that it cannot reduce to zero.

Furthermore, if $accCubeTriLinSymm$ is defined in such a way that it extracts a unique component from the inputs, then the fact that $S$ is built from $P g$ and $P! f$ ensures that this unique component does not vanish.

Therefore, combining these observations, we conclude that $accCubeTriLinSymm(P g, P g, P! f) \neq 0$ under the given conditions.

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.LineInCubic
/-!
# Parameterization in even case

Given maps `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ`, `f : Fin n → ℚ` and `a : ℚ` we form a solution to the anomaly
equations. We show that every solution can be got in this way, up to permutation, unless it, up to
permutation, lives in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis vector.

The main reference is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf

-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- Given coefficients `g` of a point in `P` and `f` of a point in `P!`, and a rational, we get a
rational `a ∈ ℚ`, we get a
point in `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear`, which we will later show extends to an anomaly
free point. -/
def parameterizationAsLinear (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols :=
  a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P' g +
  (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P!' f)

lemma parameterizationAsLinear_val (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val =
    a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P g +
    (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P! f) := by
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear]
  change a • (_ • (P' g).val + _ • (P!' f).val) = _
  rw [P'_val, P!'_val]

lemma parameterizationCharge_cube (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    accCube (2* n.succ) (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val = 0 := by
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic _ = 0
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul]
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube]
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃]
  ring

/-- The construction of a `Sol` from a `Fin n.succ → ℚ`, a `Fin n → ℚ` and a `ℚ`. -/
def parameterization (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols :=
  ⟨⟨parameterizationAsLinear g f a, fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩,
  parameterizationCharge_cube g f a⟩

lemma anomalyFree_param {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (hS : S.val = P g + P! f) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = - accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g) := by
  have hC := S.cubicSol
  rw [hS] at hC
  change (accCube (2 * n.succ)) (P g + P! f) = 0 at hC
  erw [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, P_accCube, P!_accCube] at hC
  linear_combination hC / 3

/-- A proposition on a solution which is true if `accCubeTriLinSymm (P g, P g, P! f) ≠ 0`.
In this case our parameterization above will be able to recover this point. -/
def GenericCase (S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols) : Prop := by exact?

lemma lineInCubic_expand {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols} (h : LineInCubic S) :
    ∀ (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f) (a b : ℚ),
    3 * a * b * (a * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)
    + b * accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) = 0 := by
  intro g f hS a b
  have h1 := h g f hS a b
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic (a • P g + b • P! f) = 0 at h1
  simp only [TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add] at h1
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h1
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube] at h1
  rw [← h1]

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1
  rw [hall.2.1, hall.2.2] at h2
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_add₃, h1, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃] at h2
  simpa using h2

lemma toCubic_add {charges : Type} [AddCommMonoid charges] [Module ℚ charges]

    τ.toCubic T + 3 * τ S S T + 3 * τ T T S := by

  rw [τ.swap₂ S T S, τ.swap₁ T S S, τ.swap₂ S T S, τ.swap₂ T S T, τ.swap₁ S T T, τ.swap₂ T S T]
  ring

def toCubic {charges : Type} [AddCommMonoid charges] [Module ℚ charges]
    (τ : TriLinearSymm charges) : HomogeneousCubic charges where
  toFun S := τ S S S

    simp only [smul_eq_mul]
    rw [τ.map_smul₁, τ.map_smul₂, τ.map_smul₃]

informal_statement: For any natural number \( n \) and functions \( g \) and \( f \), the cubic accumulation of \( P g + P!f \) is equal to the negative cubic accumulation of \( P!f + P!f \) under specific transformations and symmetries defined by the cubic solution property.
informal_proof:
First, we apply the cubic solution property, which allows us to express the cubic accumulation of certain terms in a transformed manner. By substituting \( P g + P!f \) into this transformation, we reframe our goal to show that the cubic accumulation of these combined terms is zero under specific conditions. This leverages known properties of the `TriLinearSymm` and `accCube` functions, which govern how cubic accumulations behave with respect to symmetries and operator applications.

Next, we systematically apply the `P_accCube` and `P!_accCube` lemmas to break down the cubic accumulation of the combined terms. Similarly, we exploit the symmetry provided by `TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add` to further decompose and simplify the expressions. These steps allow us to decompose the complex accumulation into more manageable components, revealing the relationship between `g`, `f`, and their interactions within the `accCube` framework.

Through this decomposition, we observe that when `P!f` is doubled, the resulting expression inherently carries a negative sign in relation to the original formulation involving both `g` and `f`. This negative sign arises naturally from the inherent symmetries and the cumulative properties of the `accCube` function, as elucidated by our earlier transformations.

Finally, by combining these decomposed terms and aligning their coefficients appropriately (as indicated by the linear combination and scaling by one-third), we establish the desired equality. This completes the proof that the cubic accumulation of the sum \( P g + P!f \) under `accCube` is indeed the negative accumulation of twice \( P!f \) under the same function.

import HepLean.AnomalyCancellation.PureU1.Even.LineInCubic
/-!
# Parameterization in even case

Given maps `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ`, `f : Fin n → ℚ` and `a : ℚ` we form a solution to the anomaly
equations. We show that every solution can be got in this way, up to permutation, unless it, up to
permutation, lives in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis vector.

The main reference is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf

-/

namespace PureU1
namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- Given coefficients `g` of a point in `P` and `f` of a point in `P!`, and a rational, we get a
rational `a ∈ ℚ`, we get a
point in `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear`, which we will later show extends to an anomaly
free point. -/
def parameterizationAsLinear (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols :=
  a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P' g +
  (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P!' f)

lemma parameterizationAsLinear_val (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val =
    a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P g +
    (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P! f) := by
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear]
  change a • (_ • (P' g).val + _ • (P!' f).val) = _
  rw [P'_val, P!'_val]

lemma parameterizationCharge_cube (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    accCube (2* n.succ) (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val = 0 := by
  change accCubeTriLinSymm.toCubic _ = 0
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear_val, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul,
    TriLinearSymm.toCubic_add, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul, HomogeneousCubic.map_smul]
  erw [P_accCube, P!_accCube]
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₁, accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₂,
    accCubeTriLinSymm.map_smul₃]
  ring

/-- The construction of a `Sol` from a `Fin n.succ → ℚ`, a `Fin n → ℚ` and a `ℚ`. -/
def parameterization (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :
    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols :=
  ⟨⟨parameterizationAsLinear g f a, fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩,
  parameterizationCharge_cube g f a⟩

lemma anomalyFree_param {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).Sols}
    (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (hS : S.val = P g + P! f) :
    accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f) = - accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g) := by
  exact?

  a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P' g +

    (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P! f) := by

lemma lineInCubicPerm_swap {S : (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols}
    (LIC : LineInCubicPerm S) :
    ∀ (j : Fin n) (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (_ : S.val = Pa g f),
      (S.val (evenShiftSnd j) - S.val (evenShiftFst j))
      * accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (basis!AsCharges j) = 0 := by
  intro j g f h
  let S' := (FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)) S
  have hSS' : ((FamilyPermutations (2 * n.succ)).linSolRep
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j))) S = S' := rfl
  obtain ⟨g', f', hall⟩ := span_basis_swap! j hSS' g f h
  have h1 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P! (lineInCubicPerm_self LIC) g f h
  have h2 := line_in_cubic_P_P_P!
    (lineInCubicPerm_self (lineInCubicPerm_permute LIC
    (pairSwap (evenShiftFst j) (evenShiftSnd j)))) g' f' hall.1

rag.name: LinearMap.map_mul_iff
rag.content:
/-- A `LinearMap` preserves multiplication if pre- and post- composition with `LinearMap.mul` are
equivalent. By converting the statement into an equality of `LinearMap`s, this lemma allows various
specialized `ext` lemmas about `→ₗ[R]` to then be applied.

This is the `LinearMap` version of `AddMonoidHom.map_mul_iff`. -/
theorem map_mul_iff (f : A →ₗ[R] B) :
    (∀ x y, f (x * y) = f x * f y) ↔
      (LinearMap.mul R A).compr₂ f = (LinearMap.mul R B ∘ₗ f).compl₂ f :=
  Iff.symm LinearMap.ext_iff₂

and evidence of multiplicativity on pure tensors.

def algEquivOfLinearEquivTripleTensorProduct (f : (A ⊗[R] B) ⊗[R] C ≃ₗ[R] D)
    (h_mul :
      ∀ (a₁ a₂ : A) (b₁ b₂ : B) (c₁ c₂ : C),
        f ((a₁ * a₂) ⊗ₜ (b₁ * b₂) ⊗ₜ (c₁ * c₂)) = f (a₁ ⊗ₜ b₁ ⊗ₜ c₁) * f (a₂ ⊗ₜ b₂ ⊗ₜ c₂))
    (h_one : f (((1 : A) ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : B)) ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : C)) = 1) :
    (A ⊗[R] B) ⊗[R] C ≃ₐ[R] D :=
  AlgEquiv.ofLinearEquiv f h_one <| f.map_mul_iff.2 <| by
    ext
    dsimp
    exact h_mul _ _ _ _ _ _

/-!
# Parameterization in even case

Given maps `g : Fin n.succ → ℚ`, `f : Fin n → ℚ` and `a : ℚ` we form a solution to the anomaly
equations. We show that every solution can be got in this way, up to permutation, unless it, up to
permutation, lives in the plane spanned by the first part of the basis vector.

The main reference is:

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04804.pdf

-/

namespace Even

open BigOperators

variable {n : ℕ}
open VectorLikeEvenPlane

/-- Given coefficients `g` of a point in `P` and `f` of a point in `P!`, and a rational, we get a
rational `a ∈ ℚ`, we get a
point in `(PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).AnomalyFreeLinear`, which we will later show extends to an anomaly
free point. -/

    (PureU1 (2 * n.succ)).LinSols :=
  a • ((accCubeTriLinSymm (P! f) (P! f) (P g)) • P' g +
  (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P!' f)

lemma parameterizationAsLinear_val (g : Fin n.succ → ℚ) (f : Fin n → ℚ) (a : ℚ) :

    (- accCubeTriLinSymm (P g) (P g) (P! f)) • P! f) := by
  rw [parameterizationAsLinear]
  change a • (_ • (P' g).val + _ • (P!' f).val) = _
  rw [P'_val, P!'_val]

    accCube (2* n.succ) (parameterizationAsLinear g f a).val = 0 := by
  exact?

lemma toCubic_add {charges : Type} [AddCommMonoid charges] [Module ℚ charges]
    (τ : TriLinearSymm charges) (S T : charges) :
    τ.toCubic (S + T) = τ.toCubic S +
    τ.toCubic T + 3 * τ S S T + 3 * τ T T S := by
  simp only [HomogeneousCubic, toCubic_apply]
  rw [τ.map_add₁, τ.map_add₂, τ.map_add₂, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃, τ.map_add₃]
  rw [τ.swap₂ S T S, τ.swap₁ T S S, τ.swap₂ S T S, τ.swap₂ T S T, τ.swap₁ S T T, τ.swap₂ T S T]
  ring

informal_statement: For any non-zero rational numbers $\lambda$ and $\mu$, and points $g$ in $\mathbb{Q}^{\Fin(n+1)}$ and $f$ in $\mathbb{Q}^{\Fin(n)}$, the linear combination $\lambda \cdot g + \mu \cdot f$ lies in the set $P'(\mathbb{Q})$, which consists of all points in $\mathbb{Q}^{\Fin(n+1)}$ that are in the kernel of the quadratic form $Q$ restricted to $P(\mathbb{Q})$.
informal_proof:
To prove that $\lambda g + \mu f \in P'(\mathbb{Q})$, we must show that $Q(\lambda g + \mu f) = 0$. Recall that $P'(\mathbb{Q})$ is defined as the kernel of $Q$ when restricted to $P(\mathbb{Q})$. 

Given that $g \in \mathbb{Q}^{\Fin(n+1)}$ and $f \in \mathbb{Q}^{\Fin(n)}$, and assuming that $Q(f) = 0$ because $f \in P(\mathbb{Q})$, we can express $Q(\lambda g + \mu f)$ using the bilinear property of the quadratic form:

\[
Q(\lambda g + \mu f) = \lambda^2 Q(g) + 2\lambda\mu B(g, f) + \mu^2 Q(f)
\]

Since $Q(f) = 0$, and assuming $B(g, f)$ also evaluates to zero due to the orthogonality of $g$ and $f$ with respect to the bilinear form $B$, the equation simplifies to:

\[
Q(\lambda g + \mu f) = \lambda^2 Q(g)
\]

For $\lambda g + \mu f$ to lie in $P'(\mathbb{Q})$, $Q(\lambda g + \mu f)$ must equal zero. This requires $Q(g) = 0$, meaning $g$ must also lie in $P(\mathbb{Q})$. Therefore, any linear combination of points in $P(\mathbb{Q})$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}$ remains in $P'(\mathbb{Q})$ because both $g$ and $f$ satisfy $Q(g) = Q(f) = 0$.
